name: Artist Walkthrough - Prarthna Singh
description:
Champion #4, 2015, Archival pigment inkjet print on archival paper, framed with museum glass
Join artist Prarthna Singh for a walkthrough of her work in Grip, Hold, Pin. Through photography, Singh explores the intersections of gender, identity, and nationhood, often turning her lens towards lives shaped by resilience and quiet acts of resistance.

In this exhibition, she documents the lives of women wrestlers, tracing their everyday routines, relationships, and aspirations beyond the arena. Her images reveal how strength is negotiated through the body, labour, and care, while reflecting on the larger social and political landscapes that shape contemporary India.

This event is in conjunction with programming for Grip, Hold, Pin.

name: Jarasandha Vadhe - Yakshagana Performance
description:
Tvarita Arts Collective India 

Jarasandha Vadhe is a well-known story from the Mahabharata. To help Yudhishthira perform the Rajasuya Yajna, Lord Krishna, along with Bhima and Arjuna, visits the powerful King Jarasandha of Magadha. A fierce duel follows between Bhima and Jarasandha, ending with the victory of good over evil through Krishna's guidance and Bhima's strength.

This Yakshagana performance features four iconic characters - Krishna, Jarasandha, Bhima, and Arjuna and brings the story to life through expressive acting, traditional music, vibrant costumes, and energetic dance. Presented by Team Yakshadegula, the performance is uniquely brought to life by an ensemble of women Yakshagana artists, celebrating both the richness of this classical storytelling tradition and the growing presence of women in the art form. 

The performance is curated by Tvarita Arts Collective India. 

This event is in conjunction with programming for Grip, Hold, Pin.

name: From Image to Practice
description:
Sweat and Soil, #008, Indrajit Khambe, 2018 Motibag Talim, Kolhapur, Maharashtra, India 35.56 cm, 53.34 cm
Join photographer Indrajit Khambe for a workshop exploring photography as a tool for observation, storytelling and long-term engagement. Drawing from his practice documenting communities, landscapes and cultural traditions across India—including his acclaimed series Sweat and Soil, featured in MAP's exhibition Grip, Hold, Pin- Khambe will reflect on his creative journey and the making of sustained photographic projects. 

Participants will explore the creative potential of mobile phone photography, discuss its possibilities and limitations, and learn practical approaches to building a meaningful photography practice.

This event is in conjunction with programming for Grip, Hold, Pin.

name: Muscular India
description:
The Street as Studio, Cop Shiva
How have the ideals of the wrestler's body changed in contemporary India? Once distinct, the worlds of traditional wrestling and modern fitness culture are increasingly intersecting. Gyms now incorporate training methods rooted in the akhara, while wrestlers present themselves through the visual language of bodybuilding and social media, cultivating physiques that are leaner, more muscular, and shaped by new forms of visibility.

In this conversation, anthropologist Michiel Baas and filmmaker Paromita Vohra explore the changing aesthetics of the body, tracing how ideas of strength, masculinity, discipline, and aspiration are being reimagined across wrestling, fitness culture, and digital media. Drawing on Baas's research, the discussion considers what these shifting bodily practices reveal about contemporary India and the evolving relationship between tradition, performance, and identity.

This event is in conjunction with programming for Grip, Hold, Pin.

name: Photo Talk - Prarthna Singh
description:
Champion #4, 2015, Archival pigment inkjet print on archival paper, framed with museum glass, 12.5 x 10 inches 
Through her photographs, Prarthna examines the body as a site of discipline, resilience, vulnerability, and self-expression, asking how femininity is continually reimagined in spaces traditionally coded as masculine.

The session will explore the intersections of gender, performance, nationhood, and representation, while offering insight into the ethics of long-form documentary practice and the relationships that emerge through sustained image-making. 

Through this photo talk, we will discuss her practice of building long-term relationships with the people whose lives are documented, and how photography can illuminate questions of gender, embodiment, power, and expression in contemporary India.

name: Artist Walkthrough - Indrajit Khambe
description:
Image Credits: Indrajit Khambe
Join photographer Indrajit Khambe for a walkthrough of Grip, Hold, Pin, where he will discuss the making of his acclaimed series Sweat and Soil.

Through reflections on his long-term engagement with wrestling communities, Khambe will share insights into his photographic practice, creative process, and the stories behind the images, offering a deeper understanding of the exhibition and the lives it documents.

name: Alaikadal
description: Alaikadal (meaning "the deep sea") is a powerful dance-theatre production inspired by the lives of South India's traditional coastal fishing communities. Through movement, music and evocative storytelling, director and choreographer Junafar Juno, himself from a fishing community, brings to the stage stories of labour, survival and belonging that are rarely documented, honouring a way of life sustained through collective effort and an enduring relationship with nature.

name: Curating a Dispersed Epic
description:
Rama and Lakshmana with her sage Vishvamitra from the " Shangri" Ramayana, c. 1700.
Northern India, Pahari kingdoms.
The “Shangri” Ramayana has intrigued scholars and collectors for over a century. Created around 1700 for a royal patron in the Pahari kingdoms, this illustrated manuscript is among the most ambitious visual retellings of the Ramayana. Yet, despite its significance, its origins and production have long remained a mystery.

In this talk, art historian Sonya Rhie Mace presents research based on previously unpublished paintings that reshapes our understanding of the manuscript. Her findings reveal a far greater number of folios and artistic styles than previously recognised, suggesting that the manuscript was created through a collaborative network of artists working across the Pahari region, spanning present-day Himachal Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir. The talk also traces how this once-unified manuscript became dispersed across collections over time, and how new discoveries are helping to reconstruct both its visual narrative and the artistic networks behind its creation. Join us to explore these illustrated manuscripts and the new perspectives it offers on Pahari painting and artistic collaboration.

This programme at MAP is part of A Closer Look, a monthly series of research-focused talks by artists, curators and art historians focusing on visual cultures of South Asia.

name: Curator walkthrough - Grip, Hold, Pin
description:
Folio from a ragamala series: Desakh Ragini, Unknown, Late 19th Century, Opaque watercolour on paper, H. 28.5 cm, W. 20.4 cm, Jaipur, Rajasthan, India, PTG.01140
Join Aayati Sengupta, Curator of Grip, Hold, Pin, for the first walkthrough of the exhibition. Through a close reading of the works on view, the walkthrough will explore wrestling as more than a sport—as a site where discipline, kinship, identity and everyday life converge. Drawing on photography, archival material and moving image, Grip, Hold, Pin traces the histories and lived experiences that shape wrestling cultures across India, inviting audiences to consider the relationships between body, labour, tradition and representation.

name: Family Day - Fifth Edition
description:
Whether you're coming with your children, grandparents, cousins, neighbours, or friends who feel like family, there's something waiting for everyone to discover together at our fifth edition of the Family Day. Wander through the museum, dive into hands-on workshops, listen to captivating stories, solve playful challenges, and explore exhibitions through activities designed for curious minds of all ages.

Family Day is an invitation to slow down, connect, and experience the museum in ways both familiar and unexpected. All you need to bring is your sense of curiosity, and the people you love sharing it with!

Schedule

Escape Room (10:00 am - 11:00 am) - Ages 13 to 18

In this Escape Room, clues hide in plain sight inside the paintings in Beneath the Turning Sky for you to solve and find your way out of the exhibition space! Join us for this mystery-filled adventure!

Dabble Playart (10:00 am - 12:00 pm) - Ages 1 to 6 

Explore sensory art and engage in open-ended creativity with the Dabble PlayArt experience with toxin-free Dabble Art supplies and tools! 

Tapestry (10:00 am - 4:00 pm) - All ages

 An all-day weaving space that invites us to slow down, be present, and find value in what we might otherwise overlook. In this session,  cloth becomes more than a woven object, it becomes a memory shaped by our hands and time.

ಇದು ದಿನವಿಡೀ ತೆರೆದಿರುವ ಟ್ಯಾಪೆಸ್ಟ್ರಿ ತಾಣ. ಇಲ್ಲಿ ಬಟ್ಟೆ ಬರೀ ನೇಯ್ದ ವಸ್ತುವಾಗಿರುವುದಿಲ್ಲ; ನಮ್ಮ ಕೈಗಳ ಸ್ಪರ್ಶ ಮತ್ತು ನಾವು ಕೊಟ್ಟ ಸಮಯ ಸೇರಿ, ಅದು ಒಂದು ನೆನಪಾಗಿ ರೂಪುಗೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತದೆ. 

Treevellers' Katte (11:00 am - 2:30 pm) - All Ages

A talk circle and sensory exploration with tree myths, stories and memories. We all have a special tree in our lives. Treevellers’ Katte is where tree-stories can be safely exhaled, for this is a space that holds trees and stories sacred.

ನಮ್ಮೆಲ್ಲರ ಜೀವನದಲ್ಲೂ ನಮಗೆ ವಿಶೇಷವಾದ ಒಂದು ಮರವಿರುತ್ತದೆ.  ಟ್ರೀವೆಲ್ಲರ್ಸ್‌ ಕಟ್ಟೆ ಅಂಥ ಮರದ ಕಥೆಗಳನ್ನು ಮುಕ್ತವಾಗಿ ಹಂಚಿಕೊಳ್ಳುವ ಜಾಗ — ಮರಗಳನ್ನೂ, ಅವುಗಳ ಕಥೆಗಳನ್ನೂ ಕಾಪಾಡುವ ಒಂದು ಸ್ಥಳ. ಎಲ್ಲ ವಯಸ್ಸಿನವರಿಗಾಗಿ ಮುಕ್ತ ಡ್ರಾಪ್-ಇನ್ ಸೆಷನ್.

Auto Akka - Auto Akka and the City's Heat: Experiences, Journeys, and Conversations (10:15 am - 11:15 am) - Ages 8 and above

Hear directly from Bengaluru’s Auto Akkas as they share their firsthand experiences of navigating rising heat and the everyday realities of life on the road. Moderated by Nithya, this open panel discussion will follow a reading of Auto Akka and the Hot Seat, a children’s illustrated storybook about increasing temperatures in Bengaluru, and conclude with an audience Q&A. 

ಬಿಸಿಲು ಹೆಚ್ಚುತ್ತಿರುವ ಈ ದಿನಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಬೆಂಗಳೂರಿನ ಆಟೋ ಅಕ್ಕಂದಿರು ಪ್ರತಿದಿನ ರಸ್ತೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ಏನೆಲ್ಲಾ ಅನುಭವಿಸುತ್ತಿದ್ದಾರೆ? ಅವರ ಮಾತುಗಳಲ್ಲೇ ಕೇಳಿ. ನಿತ್ಯಾ ಅವರ ನಿರೂಪಣೆಯಲ್ಲಿ ನಡೆಯುವ ಈ ಮುಕ್ತ ಸಂವಾದಕ್ಕೆ ‘ಆಟೋ ಅಕ್ಕ ಮತ್ತು ಹಾಟ್ ಸೀಟ್’ಎಂಬ ಮಕ್ಕಳ ಚಿತ್ರಕಥೆಯ ಓದಿನೊಂದಿಗೆ ಚಾಲನೆ ಸಿಗಲಿದೆ. ಬಳಿಕ ಆಟೋ ಅಕ್ಕಂದಿರು ತಮ್ಮ ನೈಜ ಅನುಭವಗಳನ್ನು ಹಂಚಿಕೊಳ್ಳುತ್ತಾರೆ.

Please note that this session is in Kannadaa

Philosophising with children (11:30 am - 1:30 pm) - Ages 12 and above

This Family Day at MAP, 'A room of children's philosophies' invites you to deep dive into a few of the exhibits from Beneath the Turning Sky and make them your philosophical playground. Share your perspectives on life's big questions and have a chance to listen to new perspectives. 

Handmade Accordion Picture Book Workshop (11:30 - 1:30 pm) - Ages 8 and above

In this workshop, participants will create their own wordless picture books using the accordion format. Through wordless picture books, explore creativity, visual storytelling, and the connections between language, art, and everyday life.

ಈ ಕಾರ್ಯಾಗಾರದಲ್ಲಿ, ಅಕಾರ್ಡಿಯನ್‌ ರೀತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮಡಚಬಹುದಾದ ತಮ್ಮದೇ ಚಿತ್ರಪುಸ್ತಕಗಳನ್ನು ತಯಾರಿಸಿ, ಅದರಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾತುಗಳಿಲ್ಲದೇ ಕಥೆ ಹೇಳಿ! ಚಿತ್ರಗಳ ಮೂಲಕ ಕಥೆ ಹೇಳುವಾಗ ನಮ್ಮ ಸೃಜನಶೀಲತೆ ಹೇಗೆ ಕೆಲಸ ಮಾಡುತ್ತದೆ, ಕಲೆ ಮತ್ತು ಭಾಷೆ ನಮ್ಮ ದಿನನಿತ್ಯದ ಬದುಕಿನ ಜೊತೆ ಹೇಗೆ ಬೆಸೆದುಕೊಂಡಿವೆ ಎಂಬುದನ್ನು ಕಂಡುಕೊಳ್ಳೋಣ. 

Uncommon Sense! A MAP Kids Quiz (11:45 am to 12:45 am) - Ages 8 and above

Part trivia, part detective work, part lucky guess! Here, knowing the obvious answer isn't enough. A team-based quiz where  families compete!  Explore strange facts, hidden stories, and unexpected connections in the Beneath the Turning Sky exhibition with this MAP Kids Quiz - an interactive art-themed live digital quiz experience hosted in real time.

Auto Akka - Tales from the Hot Seat (2:00 pm to 3:00 pm) - Ages 8 and above

How do we keep our city cool on scorching hot days? Join us for a fun, interactive session built around the children's illustrated book Auto Akka and the Hot Seat! And dive into a hands-on workshop after, to imagine, sketch, and design your very own climate resilient "cool" auto-rickshaws.

Please note that this session is in English

Storytelling with Vikram Sridhar! (2:00 to 3:00 pm) - All ages

 In this engaging hour-long session, theatre artist Vikram Sridhar explores the stories of different comic making traditions of India as seen in the exhibition ‘A Moving Line: 1500 Years of Indian Visual Storytelling’

Pop-Up World Cards! (3:00 pm to 5:00 pm) - All ages

Discover how paper can stand, fold, and surprise! Inspired by Beneath the Turning Sky, this quick pop-up activity invites you to think about our place in the world: the land we stand on, the stories we tell, and the communities we share it with. 

ಕಾಗದವನ್ನು ಮಡಚಿ, ನಿಲ್ಲಿಸಿ, ಅದರಿಂದ ಅಚ್ಚರಿ ಮೂಡಿಸುವುದನ್ನು ಕಂಡುಹಿಡಿಯಿರಿ! ತಿರುಗುವ ಆಕಾಶದ ಅಡಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಪ್ರದರ್ಶನದಿಂದ ಸ್ಫೂರ್ತಿ ಪಡೆದ ಈ ಚಿಕ್ಕ ಪಾಪ್-ಅಪ್ ಚಟುವಟಿಕೆಯಲ್ಲಿ, ನಾವು ಬದುಕುವ ಜಗತ್ತು, ಅದರ ಜೊತೆಗಿನ ನಮ್ಮ ಸಂಬಂಧ, ಮತ್ತು ಅದನ್ನು ನಮ್ಮೊಂದಿಗೆ ಹಂಚಿಕೊಳ್ಳುವ ಜನರ ಬಗ್ಗೆ ಹೊಸ ರೀತಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಯೋಚಿಸೋಣ. 

Robi’s Garden (3:30 to 4:30 pm) - All ages

Discover the fun-loving side of Rabindranath Tagore! BLT brings Robi-da’s delightful tales to life through this charming storytelling piece, performed by veteran BLT stalwarts Vijay Padaki and Minti Jain.

name: Knowing is Doing: Understanding Artist Rights
description:
Knowing is Doing: Understanding Artist Rights, is an interactive workshop that equips artists, students, and cultural practitioners with the knowledge and tools to navigate the legal, ethical, and professional realities of artistic practice. Through collaborative discussions, speculative role-playing and practical resources, participants explore authorship, contracts, copyright, labour, and advocacy, leaving with greater confidence to protect both their work and themselves. 

This session is conducted as part of our engagements for the MAP Youth Collective. The MAP Youth Collective is a community for young people (18-25 year olds) to engage with the arts and culture sector. The collective is for, of and by young people — to explore our shared identities and interests through art.

Registrations for this event will open closer to the 29th!

location.name: HDFC Ltd Learning Centre, HDFC Ltd Learning Centre, Lower Ground Floor, MAP, Bengaluru, India

name: Graphic Novels and Shared Spaces
description:
Image credits: Daniele Pasin
Comics and graphic novels have long occupied space in storytelling, finding ways to engage readers with complex realities through their visual narratives. This conversation between Susmita Mohanty and Daniele Pasin looks at the current state of graphic novel practice and publishing across India, France, Italy and Spain, and explores residency models like MAD-IFI asecosystems that support creators. Drawing from Susmita’s interdisciplinary practice, the discussion also considers how architecture, design, and exploration can shape visual narratives.

At its heart, the conversation asks what makes the graphic novel such a powerful medium for addressing difficult subjects, particularly conflict, memory and identity, while holding complexity, ambiguity and multiple perspectives.
